epic.title: Customer success manager twin for Example Software Co

stories.title: Account brief before a customer call
stories.statement: As a customer success manager, I want my twin to brief me on the account before each call so that I walk into the call already knowing the account.

fields.connectors_and_identity: hubspot: user identity, read, always-allow; google-drive: user identity, read, always-allow
fields.inputs: hubspot (company, contacts, deals, open tickets, notes); google-drive (account plan, last QBR deck, contract)
fields.output_and_audience: One-page account brief, internal; to none (the conversation)
fields.delivery: The output stays in the conversation or a local file.
fields.baseline: 6 per week x 30 minutes each x 8 users

acceptance: Eval from good example 1 of 2 (Shared drive 'CS examples' (invented)): the twin's output matches what a person accepted.
Eval from good example 2 of 2 (Shared drive 'CS examples' (invented)): the twin's output matches what a person accepted.
Eval from bad example 1 of 1 (Shared drive 'CS examples' (invented)): the twin does not repeat the mistake.
Plus: the skill triggers on the phrases its trigger evals list and stays quiet on the near-misses.

target.text: Target: edit_rate_below_pct: 30; minutes_saved_per_task: 15. Today: 6 per week, 30 minutes each, 8 users.

ready.note: Data class, surface, autonomy and identity are decided.
3 counted examples (2 good, 1 bad); at least 3 needed.
Every system the task uses has a decided connector: hubspot and google-drive.

tasks.title: Collect 3 examples of the task from real work, each with the result a person expects

how.text: Ask the people who do the task today for three recent, real examples of it.
Record each example's inputs and the output a person would accept as done.
Remove any data the examples must not carry into the repository, keeping their shape.

tasks.done_when: Three real examples, each with its inputs and its expected result, are stored where the evals can read them.

tasks.title: Write the evals from the examples and the story's acceptance criteria

how.text: Turn each example and each acceptance criterion into an eval case with its expected result.
Put the eval cases in the files the kit expects, next to the skill.
Run the evals once before any skill exists and keep the failing baseline.

tasks.done_when: Every acceptance criterion has at least one eval, and the evals run and fail without the skill.

tasks.title: Write the skill from the kit template until the evals pass

how.text: Copy the kit's skill template into the role plugin's skills folder, the one source of the skill for every runtime.
Rename the copy to the skill's name.
Fill in the description and the body, then rerun the evals until they pass.
On client-skill, the skill loads from the role plugin, which an Owner publishes to claude.ai, Desktop and Cowork and which reaches a signed-in Claude Code.
On managed-agents, the skill loads from the agent's skills array (skills uploaded through the Skills API), or from a mounted GitHub repo's .claude/skills folder.
On managed-agents-self-hosted, load the skill the same two ways as hosted Managed Agents (Unverified: no compendium page says where a self-hosted deployment loads skills from).
On agent-sdk, the skill is files on disk in the runner's container, loaded through settingSources; there is no API to register a skill.

On claude-code-scheduled-task, put the skill where Claude Code loads skills: the project's .claude/skills folder or a plugin (Unverified: no compendium page says which of these a scheduled task loads).
On claude-tag-routine, give the routine the skill as its instructions (Unverified: no compendium page says whether a Claude Tag routine loads org skills).

tasks.done_when: The skill sits in the role plugin, it is where the task's runtime loads it from, and every eval for the story passes.

tasks.title: Write and run the trigger evals for the skill

how.text: Install skill-creator where the evals run.
Write prompts that should and should not start the skill, as trigger evals.
Run the trigger evals and tighten the description until they pass.

tasks.done_when: The skill starts on every should-trigger prompt and on none of the should-not prompts.

tasks.title: Have a second person review the skill and its evals

how.text: Open a pull request with the skill and its evals.
Have someone other than the author review it against the definition of done.

tasks.done_when: A reviewer who did not write the skill has approved the pull request and the evals pass.

tasks.title: Publish the skill in the role plugin, which every member of the Team org gets

how.text: Add the skill to the role plugin and bump the plugin's version.
Add the role plugin to the one organisation-wide configuration, so every member gets the new version.
Write the skill's description so it says which role it is for, because there is no group target on Team.

tasks.done_when: A pilot user in the role sees the skill after the plugin updates, and its description names the role.

tasks.title: Hand the skill over to its owner

how.text: Show the skill owner where the skill lives: its folder in the role plugin, the one source for every runtime.
Show them how to change an instruction in the skill and add an eval case for the change.
Name who reviews a change before it is published: someone other than its author.
Have the skill owner make one change while the engineer watches.

tasks.done_when: The skill owner has made one change to the skill with the engineer watching.

tasks.title: Connect it by following the kit's runbook for this connector (hubspot)

how.text: Check the runbook's prerequisites, including who must approve the connector.
Follow the runbook's steps to add the connector and set each tool as the story's tool tasks say.
Run the runbook's checks with a pilot user before the task is built.
Record the hand-over the runbook asks for in the customer's folder.

tasks.done_when: A pilot user has connected with the planned identity, each tool is set as the story's tool tasks say, and the runbook's checks pass.

tasks.title: Connect it by following the kit's runbook for this connector (google-drive)

how.text: Check the runbook's prerequisites, including who must approve the connector.
Follow the runbook's steps to add the connector and set each tool as the story's tool tasks say.
Run the runbook's checks with a pilot user before the task is built.
Record the hand-over the runbook asks for in the customer's folder.

tasks.done_when: A pilot user has connected with the planned identity, each tool is set as the story's tool tasks say, and the runbook's checks pass.

tasks.title: Set the connector tool to Always allow, as the levelled tools list says (hubspot-read)

how.text: Open the connector's page in the Claude org and find the tool.
Set the tool to Always allow and record the change.

tasks.done_when: The tool is set to Always allow in the Claude org, as levelled.json says.

tasks.title: Set the connector tool to Always allow, as the levelled tools list says (google-drive-read)

how.text: Open the connector's page in the Claude org and find the tool.
Set the tool to Always allow and record the change.

tasks.done_when: The tool is set to Always allow in the Claude org, as levelled.json says.

tasks.title: Gather the evidence to move the task up to level 2, act with approval

how.text: Show the evals pass reliably at the current level.
Bring a month of scorecard results, with the edit rate, to the business owner.

tasks.done_when: The business owner has approved the move to level 2 on scorecard evidence, and the tool settings are changed.

tasks.title: Gather the evidence to move the task up to level 3, act within an allowlist

how.text: Confirm every allowlisted action can be undone or stays internal.
Show a stable eval pass rate, a low edit rate and few rejections at level 2.
List the tools to set to Always allow and keep every other tool on Needs approval.

tasks.done_when: The business owner has approved the allowlist on scorecard evidence, and only those tools are Always allow.

tasks.title: Confirm the unverified fact behind this decision with Anthropic or the vendor before build (connectors.google-drive)

how.text: Find the Unverified mark on the page the decision cites in levelled.json.
Ask Anthropic or the vendor in writing, using the partner questions list.
Record the answer with its source and level the card again.

tasks.done_when: The fact is confirmed in writing with a source, or the decision is changed so it no longer rests on it.

tasks.title: Resolve warning memory-poisoning-risk: keep memory writes to controlled steps for the task that reads untrusted input

how.text: Explain how untrusted input can poison memory, and that memory on claude.ai is one org-wide switch.
Keep role knowledge in reviewed skills and build the task so it never writes memory; only controlled steps write it.
If the org cannot keep memory writes to controlled steps, ask the Owner to switch memory off org-wide.

tasks.done_when: The evals show the task writes nothing to memory, its role knowledge lives in reviewed skills, and the org's memory setting is agreed.

tasks.title: Resolve warning confidential-standard-retention: set custom retention or record the customer's acceptance

how.text: Explain that page 10 requires custom retention for confidential data, otherwise local sessions are kept 6 years.
On Enterprise, set custom retention; on Team, record that the customer accepts standard retention.

tasks.done_when: Custom retention is set, or the customer's acceptance of standard retention is recorded.

stories.title: Follow-up email after a customer call, and a call note in HubSpot
stories.statement: As a customer success manager, I want my twin to draft the follow-up email and the call note for HubSpot so that the follow-up is out the same afternoon.

fields.connectors_and_identity: google-drive: user identity, read, always-allow; hubspot: user identity, write, blocked; gmail: user identity, write, blocked
fields.output_and_audience: Draft follow-up email, which the manager sends, and a call note on the HubSpot record, external; to a draft in the conversation; the HubSpot company record
fields.delivery: A person sends or files it: the twin produces a draft, hubspot-create and gmail-send are Blocked at the starting level, and they open at level 2.
fields.baseline: 6 per week x 25 minutes each x 8 users
constraints: I want to approve the note before it's created.

acceptance: Eval from good example 1 of 2 (Shared drive 'CS examples' (invented)): the twin's output matches what a person accepted.
Eval from good example 2 of 2 (Shared drive 'CS examples' (invented)): the twin's output matches what a person accepted.
Eval from bad example 1 of 1 (Shared drive 'CS examples' (invented)): the twin does not repeat the mistake.
Keeps: I want to approve the note before it's created.
Plus: the skill triggers on the phrases its trigger evals list and stays quiet on the near-misses.
Plus: the twin writes nothing to the CRM at the starting level; a person files the result.

Add the count of twin-written changes to the monthly scorecard.

When the task moves up a level, keep the write tools Blocked for people on unmanaged devices, or get the customer's written acceptance of the write and set them to Needs approval, never Always allow.

tasks.done_when: The write tools are Blocked at the starting level, and the customer's written acceptance is recorded before any of them opens for people on unmanaged devices.

tasks.done_when: The send tool is Blocked at the starting level, never Always allow, and the task's ceiling is level 2 or below.

tasks.title: Resolve warning untrusted-input-with-send: keep the send tool Blocked now, and approved by a person once it opens

tasks.done_when: Custom retention is set, or the customer's acceptance of standard retention is recorded.

stories.title: Renewal quote email to the customer
stories.statement: As a customer success manager, I want my twin to draft the renewal quote email from the HubSpot deal so that I only check the figures and send it.

fields.inputs: hubspot (renewal deal, line items, products, quote)
fields.output_and_audience: Draft renewal quote email, which the manager checks and sends from Gmail, external; to none (a draft in the conversation)
fields.delivery: The output stays in the conversation or a local file.
fields.baseline: 2 per week x 40 minutes each x 8 users
constraints: I check the figures before I send.

acceptance: Eval from good example 1 of 2 (Shared drive 'CS examples' (invented)): the twin's output matches what a person accepted.
Eval from good example 2 of 2 (Shared drive 'CS examples' (invented)): the twin's output matches what a person accepted.
Eval from bad example 1 of 1 (Shared drive 'CS examples' (invented)): the twin does not repeat the mistake.
Keeps: I check the figures before I send.
Plus: the skill triggers on the phrases its trigger evals list and stays quiet on the near-misses.

target.text: Target: edit_rate_below_pct: 30; minutes_saved_per_task: 15. Today: 2 per week, 40 minutes each, 8 users.

ready.note: Data class, surface, autonomy and identity are decided.
3 counted examples (2 good, 1 bad); at least 3 needed.
Every system the task uses has a decided connector: hubspot.

tasks.title: Collect 3 examples of the task from real work, each with the result a person expects

how.text: Ask the people who do the task today for three recent, real examples of it.
Record each example's inputs and the output a person would accept as done.
Remove any data the examples must not carry into the repository, keeping their shape.

tasks.done_when: Three real examples, each with its inputs and its expected result, are stored where the evals can read them.

tasks.title: Write the evals from the examples and the story's acceptance criteria

how.text: Turn each example and each acceptance criterion into an eval case with its expected result.
Put the eval cases in the files the kit expects, next to the skill.
Run the evals once before any skill exists and keep the failing baseline.

tasks.done_when: Every acceptance criterion has at least one eval, and the evals run and fail without the skill.

tasks.title: Write the skill from the kit template until the evals pass

how.text: Copy the kit's skill template into the role plugin's skills folder, the one source of the skill for every runtime.
Rename the copy to the skill's name.
Fill in the description and the body, then rerun the evals until they pass.
On client-skill, the skill loads from the role plugin, which an Owner publishes to claude.ai, Desktop and Cowork and which reaches a signed-in Claude Code.
On managed-agents, the skill loads from the agent's skills array (skills uploaded through the Skills API), or from a mounted GitHub repo's .claude/skills folder.
On managed-agents-self-hosted, load the skill the same two ways as hosted Managed Agents (Unverified: no compendium page says where a self-hosted deployment loads skills from).
On agent-sdk, the skill is files on disk in the runner's container, loaded through settingSources; there is no API to register a skill.

On claude-code-scheduled-task, put the skill where Claude Code loads skills: the project's .claude/skills folder or a plugin (Unverified: no compendium page says which of these a scheduled task loads).
On claude-tag-routine, give the routine the skill as its instructions (Unverified: no compendium page says whether a Claude Tag routine loads org skills).
Make the skill keep these rules from the interviews, in the interviewee's words: I check the figures before I send..

tasks.done_when: The skill sits in the role plugin, it is where the task's runtime loads it from, and every eval for the story passes.

tasks.title: Write and run the trigger evals for the skill

how.text: Install skill-creator where the evals run.
Write prompts that should and should not start the skill, as trigger evals.
Run the trigger evals and tighten the description until they pass.

tasks.done_when: The skill starts on every should-trigger prompt and on none of the should-not prompts.

tasks.title: Have a second person review the skill and its evals

how.text: Open a pull request with the skill and its evals.
Have someone other than the author review it against the definition of done.

tasks.done_when: A reviewer who did not write the skill has approved the pull request and the evals pass.

tasks.title: Publish the skill in the role plugin, which every member of the Team org gets

how.text: Add the skill to the role plugin and bump the plugin's version.
Add the role plugin to the one organisation-wide configuration, so every member gets the new version.
Write the skill's description so it says which role it is for, because there is no group target on Team.

tasks.done_when: A pilot user in the role sees the skill after the plugin updates, and its description names the role.

tasks.title: Hand the skill over to its owner

how.text: Show the skill owner where the skill lives: its folder in the role plugin, the one source for every runtime.
Show them how to change an instruction in the skill and add an eval case for the change.
Name who reviews a change before it is published: someone other than its author.
Have the skill owner make one change while the engineer watches.

tasks.done_when: The skill owner has made one change to the skill with the engineer watching.

tasks.title: Connect it by following the kit's runbook for this connector (hubspot)

how.text: Check the runbook's prerequisites, including who must approve the connector.
Follow the runbook's steps to add the connector and set each tool as the story's tool tasks say.
Run the runbook's checks with a pilot user before the task is built.
Record the hand-over the runbook asks for in the customer's folder.

tasks.done_when: A pilot user has connected with the planned identity, each tool is set as the story's tool tasks say, and the runbook's checks pass.

tasks.done_when: The tool is set to Always allow in the Claude org, as levelled.json says.

how.text: Show the evals pass reliably at the current level.
Bring a month of scorecard results, with the edit rate, to the business owner.

tasks.done_when: The business owner has approved the move to level 2 on scorecard evidence, and the tool settings are changed.

how.text: Explain that page 10 requires custom retention for confidential data, otherwise local sessions are kept 6 years.
On Enterprise, set custom retention; on Team, record that the customer accepts standard retention.

tasks.done_when: Custom retention is set, or the customer's acceptance of standard retention is recorded.

spikes.title: What could start C5 on the escalation itself, without a person: a Zendesk trigger calling a hosted agent, or a Slack…
spikes.question: What could start C5 on the escalation itself, without a person: a Zendesk trigger calling a hosted agent, or a Slack alert? Until then the manager starts it.
